thread.title: President Trump Designates Oval Office A National Monument In Surprise Proclamation
thread.title_full: President Trump Designates Oval Office A National Monument In Surprise Proclamation

author: @100percFEDUP
title: President Trump Designates Oval Office A National Monument In Surprise Proclamation
text:
President Donald Trump has signed a proclamation establishing the Oval Office as a national monument, placing America’s most famous working office under a new preservation plan.
The designation reaches beyond the room seen in televised presidential addresses. It also covers the Outer Oval Office and the Cabinet Room.
SIGNED: Designating the Oval Office as a National Monument, protecting the historic office for good. 🇺🇸
[pic.twitter.com/x10uKg1AUe]— The White House (@WhiteHouse)
[November 6, 2026]
The proclamation invokes the Antiquities Act and identifies the protected spaces by room number: the Oval Office in Room 110, the Outer Oval Office in Rooms 106 and 108, and the Cabinet Room in Room 105.
Trump’s order directs the Interior secretary, acting through the National Park Service, to create a management plan with the White House Office of Administration and other relevant agencies.
That plan must prioritize the rooms’ structural and significant architectural features. It must also require documentation, review and consideration of alternatives before any substantial alteration or demolition.
The secretary must evaluate proposed changes against the monument’s national significance and coordinate with the Committee for the Preservation of the White House. The proclamation describes the designated rooms as the smallest area compatible with protecting the historic objects at issue.
The order takes effect as a preservation directive, not a transfer of the presidency’s daily control over its workspace. It leaves existing statutory exemptions for the White House untouched and expressly preserves Congress’s authority over federal property.
Trump described the action in blunt terms while signing it inside the Oval Office.
TRUMP DECLARES THE OVAL OFFICE A NATIONAL MONUMENT!
“It will not be allowed to be touched by anybody.”
President Trump signed a proclamation in the Oval Office declaring it a national monument, and said he’s sending it to Congress to be ratified.
“We had the President of China…
[pic.twitter.com/pfypytB9c8]— Townhall.com (@townhallcom)
[November 5, 2026]
The text grounds the designation in the history carried inside those walls.
It notes that the room’s oval design first appeared in the West Wing under President William Howard Taft and reached its present location and form during Franklin D. Roosevelt’s administration.
For almost a century, presidents have used the room to receive foreign leaders, direct the executive branch and make decisions with consequences far beyond Washington.
The White House fact sheet says the goal is preservation, proper care and management. It calls the Oval Office one of the nation’s most recognizable and historically significant spaces.
The administration’s account emphasizes that the office has hosted heads of state and served as the setting for decisions with national and international consequences. Its value comes from both the architecture and the uninterrupted association with the presidency.
The White House and its grounds already carry National Historic Landmark status. The new action argues that the Oval Office deserves distinct recognition and protective management as its own historic structure of national significance.
The fact sheet places the proclamation inside Trump’s broader effort to restore and preserve historic places in Washington. Here, the practical result is a named federal official, a required management plan and a review process before anyone attempts a major structural change.
The proclamation is precise about what the designation does not freeze. A president may still redecorate, choose furnishings, and make ordinary operational or security changes that do not substantially damage the monument’s historic structure or architectural character.
It also states that Congress retains its authority over federal property. In other words, the order creates a formal preservation framework without pretending that a working presidential office can be sealed in amber.
🚨 JUST IN: President Trump just EMERGED in the Oval Office with a red "VETO" hat on the Resolute Desk to sign a document ensuring the Oval Office and Cabinet room are a LANDMARK that can't be demolished by future presidents
Good.
This is American history. Upgrade it, NEVER…
[pic.twitter.com/3K3a9wubay]— Eric Daugherty (@EricLDaugh)
[November 5, 2026]
The Oval Office has long been protected as part of the White House National Historic Landmark. Trump’s proclamation gives the office itself separate recognition and directs federal officials to treat its preservation as a specific responsibility.
Presidents will continue to put their own stamp on the room. The walls, shape and historic character now have an additional line of defense.

The new action argues that the Oval Office deserves distinct recognition and protective management as its own historic structure of national significance.
